newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan cotton rates rise on exporters' demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan cotton rates rise on exporters' demand.

text.p: Pakistan cotton rates rose on Wednesday amid demand from exporters beefing up their stocks on reports that recent rains could delay the arrival of 1997/98 (July-June) crop, dealers said.
"Prices should rise as reports say only limited stocks of good quality cotton from this year's crop remain with ginners while some stocks have been damaged by rain," one dealer said.
In the kerb market, NIAB-78 was traded at 2,200 rupees ($54.33) per maund (37.32 k.g.), K-68 at 2,050 rupees and MNH-93 at 2,130 rupees, dealers said.
